title: terraform: refactor private state layout + GPU node-pool IAM/networking for Private deployments
author: Asha Patel
description: Refactor terraform modules used for Private deployments to introduce a clearer state layout, tighten IAM for GPU node pools, and clean up networking defaults for VPC-based installs. Motivation: customers running Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments have seen operational friction when upgrading or migrating state (duplicate remote state files), and we needed more explicit least-privilege IAM roles for GPU node pools and predictable subnetwork allocation for on-prem proxies. This PR consolidates the state backend layout (per-environment + per-region prefixes), adds migration helpers, splits GPU node-pool IAM into dedicated role modules, and clarifies networking defaults in the examples. The description below summarizes the changes, migration plan, and risk/rollback notes. Changes: - New modules/state/backend.tf: introduce environment and region-based key_prefix structure, configurable lock table name, and clearer documentation for state pathing. - modules/gpu-node-pool: split IAM into modules/iam/gpu-node-pool-role.tf and provide minimal role bindings; added node taint/toleration defaults for GPU workloads. - modules/networking: default subnetwork allocation improved to avoid /16 conflicts with customer networks; added optional explicit CIDR ranges to examples. - scripts/state-migrate.sh: helper to move existing state to the new key prefix (wrapping terraform init and state mv where needed). - examples/private-deploy/upgrade.md: step-by-step migration and rollback instructions including sample commands and validation queries (terraform plan, state list, k8s node checks). Tests/CI: upgraded unit tests to use local backend mocks and added a CI job to run a migration dry-run. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve previous behavior when key_prefix not set, but we recommend running the migration helper to get the improved layout. Rollback: migration script keeps a copy of the original state key (suffixed .bak) and the upgrade doc includes steps to revert. Related linear items: ENG-4982 (state migration), ENG-5034 (gpu node-pool least-privilege), PM-218 (private deploy upgrade UX).

review_comments: Eve Chen: Please ensure the remote state migration preserves locks and that the lock table parameter is configurable per-org. Also request adding an automated smoke validation after migration.

Asha Patel: Responded - made lock table name configurable via var.lock_table_name and added smoke validation instructions to examples/private-deploy/upgrade.md. The migration helper now exits non-zero on validation failures.

release_notes: Refactors Terraform state layout for Private deployments (per-environment/region prefixes), adds GPU node-pool least-privilege IAM module, and provides state migration tooling and upgrade docs. Operators should run the provided migration helper before upgrading multiple clusters.
risk_and_rollback: Migration of remote state is the primary risk surface. The included state-migrate.sh creates a .bak copy of the original key and has validation checks; instructions include how to revert by restoring the original key and rerunning terraform init. We added CI migration dry-run to reduce risk. Node-pool IAM changes are additive and default to previous bindings unless the new module is explicitly used.
testing_and_validation: Added unit tests using a local backend mock and a migration dry-run CI job. Manual validation steps in examples/private-deploy/upgrade.md include: terraform init/plan, terraform state list, node readiness checks on k8s, and validate IAM bindings via cloud provider console/CLI.
